subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should managed Gateway install/refresh fail before service planning when an explicit no-auth configuration resolves outside loopback?
rationale: The patch matches an existing runtime safety boundary, but it intentionally moves failure earlier in a setup/refresh path and can require operator config action for existing invalid managed installs.

options.title: Accept earlier fail-closed install guard
options.body: Merge the PR if maintainers want managed install behavior to match the current runtime refusal with clearer remediation before service rewrite.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service refresh transcript before accepting the compatibility-sensitive guard.

options.title: Pause for broader update investigation
options.body: Keep this PR paused if maintainers want the original update-mutation claim proven and repaired in the same path.

recommendation.title: Accept earlier fail-closed install guard
recommendation.body: Merge the PR if maintainers want managed install behavior to match the current runtime refusal with clearer remediation before service rewrite.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history across Gateway auth hardening, install-token behavior, and the exposed-startup security boundary.
